svg.title: Which step should the next ADC improve?
svg.desc: An ADC binds a surface antigen, is internalized into an endosome and traffics to a lysosome for design-dependent payload release. Alternative branches show a Topo-I inhibitor acting in the nucleus and a microtubule inhibitor acting in the cytoplasm. They do not depict a dual-payload ADC. Possible failure points are blood stability, antigen heterogeneity, intracellular delivery, and payload resistance.
svg.metadata: Artifact version: ADC-20261007-R1-LAYERED-HTML-R2-1.0; parent research: ADC-20261007-R1; parent pilot: ADC-20261007-R1-VISUAL-PILOT2-1.0; source correction: remove recycling branch, replace T14 with R10 for intracellular delivery; evidence as of 2026-10-07.
svg.text: Conceptual; no product-level clinical benefit implied.
